honesty_conditions.text: Every clause of the announcement is covered by a requirement in this frame and by a test in the D2 acceptance suite; a clause without a passing test is reported as not delivered.

claims.text: Operators and calling agents (the agents CLI today; culture-rules and embodiment later) that submit work to more than one culture-agents host and need the state they read to stay true across restarts and host failures.

honesty_conditions.text: The agents CLI is the only caller D2 is tested with. culture-rules and embodiment are named as later callers and nothing in D2 is built for them alone.

claims.text: After a core restart, the core takes back live control (steer, cancel, attach) of every worker that survived it. reconcile() rebuilds the in-memory controls map through the existing reconnectWorker, and the 'reconnect' capability stops being refused.

honesty_conditions.text: Reattach is proven by killing the core process (SIGKILL, not a clean stop) while a stub-harness run is mid-turn, starting a new core, and observing a steer and a cancel take effect on that run. claims.text: Two runs can be active in one repository at the same time, each steered independently, with a stated bound on how many. The one-active-run-per-repository 'busy' rule becomes a limit check, and the 'worktree_isolation' capability reports what is actually guaranteed.

honesty_conditions.text: Two concurrent runs in one repository each return commits only on their own runs/<id> branch, and neither branch contains the other's commits. The bound is a number a caller can read, and a submit past it gets a typed refusal, not a queue that is silently created.

claims.text: Per-run isolation stays what D1 built: each run works in its own sandbox clone made from a git bundle, and its commits return into its own runs/<id> branch. The host checkout and index are never written, and no git worktree is created on the host.

honesty_conditions.text: No code path in D2 calls 'git worktree' or writes the host checkout or index. This holds only if q1 is answered 'sandbox clones are the isolation D2 means'.

hard_questions.text: Issue #2 words the D2 test as 'confirm separate worktrees'. Each run already has its own clone inside its sandbox. Is that the isolation D2 means, or do you want host-side git worktrees as well (for example to hand a result over for review)?

claims.text: A duplicate submit with the same idempotency key returns the first run instead of starting a second one, and the same key with a different request is refused as a conflict. Steer and cancel deduplicate on their keys the same way. The key index is on disk, so it holds across a restart.

honesty_conditions.text: The key index is written to disk before the submit is acknowledged, so a crash between the two cannot produce a second run for the same key. The comparison that decides 'same request' is stated in the contract, including how long a key is remembered.

claims.text: A run can ask its operator a question and wait. The question is written to the run's on-disk log, is still pending after a core restart, and 'agents runs answer' delivers the answer into the same run. A harness that cannot ask says so in its capability report.

honesty_conditions.text: At least one real harness can ask and wait without allow-all approvals. docs/d0/probe.md:286-295 lists approvals as unverified in the AI SDK adapter, so this requirement is conditional on a probe that runs before the plan; if no harness can ask, the capability is reported unsupported and the requirement is cut down to the store and the 'answer' verb against the stub.

claims.text: A submit names where the work may run, and the core admits it only when that host can take it: the harness is available, the concurrency bound has room, and the host's heat and model-gateway signals do not say hold. A signal that is missing or stale reads as unknown, never as permission and never as a hard failure of the control plane.

honesty_conditions.text: The heat and model-gateway signals are read through the interfaces heat-governor and lobes already publish, with no change to either. A test covers each of: signal says go, signal says hold, signal missing, signal stale.

claims.text: When a host halts, every run that was active on it reads 'unknown' (or a state that says the host is unreachable) to every caller, and never 'succeeded'. The rule that already holds for a dead worker on one host holds across hosts.

honesty_conditions.text: A halted host is detected by something that can be tested (a missed heartbeat or a failed request with a stated timeout), and the reader's answer never changes a run's stored terminal state: 'unknown' is a view until the host returns and reports.

claims.text: Finished runs stop accumulating: there is a way to list the runs/<id> branches a repository holds, and a rule for removing one that requires positive evidence its commits are kept elsewhere (merged, or on another ref). Unknown liveness defers removal; nothing is force-deleted.

honesty_conditions.text: Removal never runs 'git branch -D'. The evidence rule (merged into a named ref, or reachable from another ref) is checked by git itself, and a branch whose run is 'unknown' or still retained is skipped and listed as skipped.

Decided by the owner on 2026-11-25: each same-repository pull request stages <version>-dev.<run number> with --tag dev, and main publishes the real version. npm's docs confirm a staged version blocks publishing that version, that 'npm stage publish' works with a trusted publisher while approve, reject, list and view do not, and that a pre-release needs an explicit tag. They state no expiry for staged versions, so each one stays until the owner rejects it with 2FA.
